title: Cal Grant A

award.text: Pays tuition and fees; up to $15,588 a year at UC, $6,838 at CSU (2026-27)

rules.other: Low to middle family income and assets under state limits; first bachelor's or associate degree; must attend an eligible California college at least half-time; 2.4 GPA if applying from college

description: California's main grant for low and middle income students working toward an associate or bachelor's degree. It pays tuition and fees at UC, CSU, and some private colleges. If you start at a community college, the award is saved for up to 2 years until you transfer. You do not apply separately: file the FAFSA by March 2 and make sure your school sends your GPA. Also open through the California Dream Act Application.

title: Cal Grant B

award.text: Up to $1,648 a year for living costs, plus tuition from year 2 (up to $15,588 at UC, 2026-27)

rules.other: Low family income and assets under state limits; first bachelor's or associate degree; must attend an eligible California college at least half-time

description: A California grant for low income students in programs at least one year long that lead to an associate or bachelor's degree. In the first year it gives money for costs like books and living expenses. After that it also pays tuition at UC, CSU, and some private colleges. File the FAFSA by March 2, or by September 2 if you go to a community college. Also open through the California Dream Act Application.

title: Cal Grant C

award.text: Up to $1,094 for books at community colleges, or $3,009 for tuition and books at private schools

rules.other: Job or technical training program at least 8 weeks long at a California community college or eligible private career school; income and asset limits; limited number of awards

description: A California grant for students in job or technical training programs, like certificates for skilled trades or health jobs. No GPA is required. Awards are limited, so students are scored and chosen, with extra points for jobs the state needs most. If picked, you fill out a short extra form online. It can be renewed for up to 2 years. File the FAFSA by September 2. Also open through the California Dream Act Application.

title: Middle Class Scholarship

award.text: Amount varies with your college costs and other aid

rules.other: Must attend a UC, CSU, or California community college bachelor's degree program; family income and assets up to $250,000 (2026-27)

description: A California scholarship for undergraduates from low and middle income families, including students earning a teaching credential. It helps pay what is left of your college costs after other aid. The amount depends on your costs and state funding. You do not apply separately: file the FAFSA by the deadline, usually March 2. Also open through the California Dream Act Application.

title: California Chafee Grant for Foster Youth

rules.other: Current or former foster youth in foster care at least one day between ages 16 and 18; under 26 on July 1 of the award year; enrolled at least half-time

description: A grant for current and former foster youth going to college or a career or technical school. You can use it for up to 5 years. Funding is limited and paid first come, first served, so apply early. There is a one-time Chafee application that opens October 1, plus the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application every year. Also open through the California Dream Act Application.

title: California College Promise Grant

award.text: Waives community college enrollment fees ($46 per unit)

rules.other: California community college students only; based on income or receiving cash aid like CalWORKs or SSI; keep a 2.0 GPA and finish over half your classes to keep it

description: Waives enrollment fees at California community colleges for students with low income or whose families get cash aid. You can apply through the FAFSA or a short Promise Grant form at your college, and you reapply each year. To keep it, you need a 2.0 GPA and must finish more than half the classes you take. Also open through the California Dream Act Application.

title: Golden State Teacher Grant

award.text: Up to $10,000, or $20,000 for special education credentials

rules.other: Must be enrolled in a state-approved teacher credential program in a high-need field; must agree to work 2 to 4 years at a high-need California school or pay some back

description: A grant for students earning a California teaching credential in special education, math, science, industrial and technology education, bilingual teaching, or pupil services (like school counseling). In return you promise to work at a high-need California school or state preschool for 2 or 4 years, or you must pay part of it back. Awards go to students with the most need until money runs out. Apply with the grant application and the FAFSA. Also open through the California Dream Act Application.

title: Bachelor of Science Nursing Scholarship Program
sponsor: California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI)

award.text: Up to $10,000 for one year of school

rules.other: Must be enrolled in a bachelor's nursing (RN) program, at least 6 units; must agree to work 1 year full-time caring for patients at a qualifying California facility

description: A state scholarship for students in a bachelor's degree nursing program that leads to becoming a registered nurse. In return, you agree to work full-time for one year giving direct patient care at a qualifying California facility or underserved area, starting within six months of graduating. You need at least a 2.0 GPA. Apply through the HCAI funding portal.
